items.quote: If we go by S&P Global mobility, Indian hybrid and EV cars and the commercial vehicle market alone represents an addressable market of over 2.3 million vehicles, which would roughly amount to about a 24,000 crore opportunity in 2030 itself.

items.statement: JV2 (high voltage) market size estimated at Rs 24,000 crore by 2030, potentially 3x by 2035; targeting market leadership
items.quote: Market size, I did say 2030, 24,000 crores, but if you were to look at 2035, this number will be many times that. It will be maybe 3 times that, and that is what we are looking at.

items.statement: JV2 capex intensity low: Rs 1 capex yields Rs 11-12 revenue for high voltage motor and controller business
items.quote: For ₹1 of capex, how much revenue is the thumb rule? Sat Mohan Gupta: It will be at least 11-12

items.statement: EV demand strong; not constrained by demand but by OEM supply chain bottlenecks; India fastest growing EV market globally
items.quote: EV is in a way, right now, we are not constrained by demand. Actually, all our OEMs are not constrained by demand. They are constrained by their own supply chain challenges.

items.statement: Suspension motors growing fastest among existing products; traction motors second fastest
items.quote: I think suspension motors are growing the fastest rate. The traction motor would be the second.

items.statement: Rare earth magnet restrictions persist; shifted to light rare earth alternatives with no impact on EV traction motor growth
items.quote: Heavy rare earth magnets cannot be imported. Almost all that we do today is with light rare earth alternatives, and it's working fine.

items.statement: JV1 (2W/3W) to kickstart first; JV2 (high voltage) to follow; global expansion planned in phase 2 for JV2
items.quote: The first JV is the one which will kickstart, faster. Yeah.

items.statement: Europe electrifying fast (BEV, strong hybrids, PHEVs); US shifting to hybrids but EV growth still phenomenal this year
items.quote: Europe is electrifying very fast. I mean, whether it be fully BEV or, whether it be strong hybrids or plug-in hybrids, they are actually accelerating quite fast.

items.statement: New technology ramp timeline: Year 1-3 no revenue, Year 4 first $1 revenue, Year 5 $10M, Year 7-8 $100M; robotics expected faster
items.quote: First 3 years when you make a new product or get into a new technology, you make no money. Year 4, you see your 1st $1 of revenue. Year 5, you start making the 1st $10 million odd dollar number, and year 7 or year 8 is when it becomes a $100 million business.

items.statement: Targets 15-20% revenue CAGR over next 5 years for both top and bottom line
items.quote: we can grow in the range of 15% to 20% CAGR. So 1 year can be here and there because of XYZ reasons. But the way India demand is growing and the plant that the capacities that we have, eventually plant will ramp up and we can have a CAGR growth of 15% to 20% for the next 5 years.

items.statement: Board approved INR600 crore capex for Epoxy Resin & Formulations (125,000 TPA) and Multipurpose Plant
items.quote: I'm also pleased to announce that our Board has approved a strategic capex plan for 2 new projects. We are entering into the Epoxy Resin & Formulations with a capacity of 125,000 tons per annum and setting up a multipurpose plant.

items.statement: Targets INR500 crore revenue from Multipurpose Plant (chlorotoluenes & ECH derivatives) by FY29-FY30
items.quote: our target is to reach -- once the multipurpose plant will be commissioned, our target is to reach all the derivatives, specialty product portfolio, which we are producing in multipurpose plant, along with the chlorotoluene derivatives, we wanted to close to around INR500 crores revenue we would like to target.

items.statement: Chlorotoluenes + MPP combined EBITDA margin estimated at 22-23% at peak utilization
items.quote: So the estimated margin would be in the range of 22%, 23% kind of thing. And again, once we commission the plant, it will take time to ramp up, maybe 1.5 or 2 years' time to reach the optimum level utilization levels.

items.statement: No further captive power investment; energy needs to be met via solar-wind hybrid PPAs (40 MW contracted, more to come)
items.quote: We are not going to invest further in the captive power plant. Whatever we are going further, the energy requirement is going to be catered from solar and wind hybrid agreement, which we are doing with the different suppliers on a long-term basis.

items.statement: Caustic soda utilization ~75% due to short-term oversupply; long-term demand supported by alumina expansion and downstream growth
items.quote: caustic, I believe because of the way the alumina expansion is happening in the country. So, we believe we are going to be net import of caustic continuously in India, irrespective of the capacity addition will happen gradually.

items.statement: KFC store expansion guidance maintained at 60-80 stores for the year
items.quote: The earlier guidance for KFC in terms of 60 to 80 stores in a year remains the same. That continues. No change in that particular guidance.

items.statement: Sri Lanka store opening guidance unchanged despite profitability challenges
items.quote: So the guidance remains for this particular year.

items.statement: Sri Lanka profitability normalization expected in a couple of quarters
items.quote: At least a couple of quarters away.

items.statement: KFC new store payback and ADS metrics remain healthy supporting 60-80 store expansion
items.quote: If we feel those strike rates are dropping, we would immediately drop our store expansion plan. But over the last 2 to 3 years for KFC, we have continued to perform reasonably well.

items.statement: KFC restaurant EBITDA margin at 16.9%, up 120 bps YoY despite energy cost pressures
items.quote: The overall restaurant EBITDA came at very healthy 16.9%.

items.statement: Pizza Hut restaurant EBITDA margin at -3.6%, down 110 bps YoY due to higher energy costs
items.quote: However, higher energy cost impacted the restaurant EBITDA, which came at loss of 3.6%, down by 110 basis points.

items.statement: KFC took 2% price increase during Q1 FY27 in two instalments
items.quote: We have taken it in two instalments. One percent was taken in April, 0.5% to 1% was taken in June.

items.statement: Price hikes restricted to 50-60% of inflation, rest managed via supply chain efficiencies
items.quote: We have always called out that we never take price hikes exactly same as inflation. So we would typically restrict our price hikes to 50% to 60% of the inflation.

items.statement: Demand environment unchanged; KFC SSSG driven by value strategy not macro improvement
items.quote: I don't think there's been any material improvement in the demand environment. I would say it has remained similar.

items.statement: KFC dine-in and takeaway mix improved from 57% to 59% driven by value campaigns
items.quote: Dine-in and takeaway sales for KFC improved from 57% to 59%. This is on basis of the strong dine-in takeaway value campaigns.

items.statement: Sri Lanka profitability susceptible to currency depreciation, wage inflation, and geopolitical fuel costs
items.quote: Cost of sales increased because of the depreciation of the Sri Lankan rupee, minimum wage increase and cost of utilities and fuel increasing because of the geopolitical crisis in the Middle East.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 18.3%, within guided framework; normalized margins in line with long-term 20% expectation
items.quote: Q1 EBITDA was INR1,032 million. It was up 8.5% year-on-year and 3% quarter-on-quarter at a margin of 18.3%, which is within the framework that we had guided for Q1 when we met last.

items.statement: Organic constant currency growth 5% YoY excluding RECO contract; overall constant currency growth 11.4% YoY and 2.9% QoQ
items.quote: Normalizing for that, our overall constant currency growth for Q1 FY27 came in at 18% and the organic constant currency growth is 5% year-on-year.

items.statement: Revenue visibility improved to USD462 million, up 19% YoY; signed 3 new long-term annuity contracts, total annuity clients now 113
items.quote: Our contract pipeline continues to be strong. The revenue visibility improved to USD462 million. It was up 19% year-on-year from USD388 million a year ago.

items.statement: Actively evaluating acquisitions; significant capital allocation to AI infrastructure build-out; consistent dividend policy maintained
items.quote: A, we are actively looking at acquisitions. Second, as we have mentioned in the past and I mentioned earlier, we have a significant investment going into AI and AI-related build-out of infrastructure. So those are two significant areas that will consume capital.

items.statement: SweetRush phased margin buildup impacting near-term margins; AI investments continuing but returns becoming more material
items.quote: The year-on-year margin movement reflects the phased margin buildup of SweetRush together with the continued investment in AI as well as the sunsetting of the North American real estate contract.

items.statement: Targeting 25% blended EBITDA margin over next few years, currently on track
items.quote: So, the target for the company overall is to achieve an EBITDA margin of 25% in the next few years, and we are right now on track to achieve that.

items.statement: INR48 crore budgeted for skid assembly capacity expansion from 2,000 to 15,000 units per annum
items.quote: And for that, we have budgeted the capex of INR48 crores. So, the entire capex would be utilized to increase the capacity from 2,000 to 15,000.

items.statement: INR54 crore budgeted for flexible hose capacity expansion from 16.5 to 20 million meters per annum, completion by Q3 FY27
items.quote: And the budgeted capex for the same for the entire was around INR54 crores. The plan -- so some of it was spent in FY25, some of it was spent in FY26 and now the remaining would be completed in FY27.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 23.04% (+468 bps YoY), PAT margin ~13% (+440 bps YoY), cash profit margin 18.25% (+278 bps YoY)
items.quote: Our EBITDA stood at INR33.5 crores, which is up by 116% on a year-on-year basis with margins expanding by 468 basis points as compared to the same quarter in last year to 23.04%.

items.statement: Flexible hose margins 16-20%, assemblies 22-26%, blended ~22-23%; skid margins at company average level
items.quote: When we sell the flexible hose just in the hose form, margins range between 16% to 20%. And when we sell the assemblies, the margins range anywhere between 22% to 26% margins.

items.statement: Expecting international skid assembly orders in FY27; fire hose assembly commercialization by end of Q1 or start of Q2 FY27 for international supply
items.quote: Yes. So, we are definitely on track. And in this financial year, we'll definitely have business coming in from international market.

items.statement: Skid assemblies contributed 23% of Q1 revenue (INR32.4 crore); flexible hose 37%, assemblies/fittings 63% of hose vertical
items.quote: Revenue from SFN Skid Assemblies reached INR32.4 crores in this quarter, which is contributing to approximately 23% of the total revenue.

items.statement: Flexible hose peak revenue potential INR650-675 crore at 70% assembly mix and peak utilization
items.quote: With the -- at the peak utilization and assuming that 70% of the sales comes in from the assemblies, we are looking at a top line of anywhere between INR650 crores to INR675 crores.

items.statement: Skid capacity expansion to 15,000 units by Q3 FY27 (Oct-Nov), targeting 80% optimal utilization in FY28
items.quote: No. About 80% is the optimum utilization.

items.statement: Logistics costs increased significantly in Q1 due to West Asia crisis impacting margins sequentially
items.quote: Also to add to that, just because the -- barring the material cost in the last -- in the Q1, if you also would see that logistics cost also has increased because of the crisis that has happened in West Asia.

items.statement: ~40 skids per megawatt of liquid-cooled IT load; 9 GW India data centre pipeline implies large addressable market
items.quote: About 40-odd skids go into 1 megawatt on an average.

items.statement: Hyd-Air revenue INR7 crore, metal bellows INR3 crore in Q1; bellows sales uptick expected in next 2 quarters
items.quote: So, the revenue from Hyd-Air in the last quarter was around INR7 crores. And the revenue from the metal bellows was about INR3 crores in this quarter, in Q1.

items.statement: Skid assembly facility machines fungible for other flow control applications (HVAC, ports) if data centre demand tapers
items.quote: So, some of these machines can be utilized for bellows. A lot of these machines can be utilized for providing flow control solutions for other industrial applications as well.

items.statement: FY27 loan growth guidance of 22% and FY29 loan book target of INR 16,000 crores plus
items.quote: As we look forward, the momentum of the first quarter marks an important step towards Vision 2029 and making us well positioned to achieve the target FY29 loan book of INR16,000 crores plus and 22% growth in FY27.

items.statement: ROA target of 1.35-1.4% for FY27 and 1.6% plus by FY29; ROE target 15% plus by FY29
items.quote: We expect further ROTA expansion and targeting to make it towards 1.4% in FY27 and 1.6% plus by FY29 and ROE expansion to 15% plus by FY29.

items.statement: NIM improved to 4.21% in Q1 FY27 from 4.06% in Q4 FY26 driven by deposit repricing and higher CD ratio
items.quote: Net interest margin has improved to 4.21% against 4.06% in the previous quarter and 4.06% a year ago. The same is supported by a decline in the deposit cost on repricing, coupled with acceleration in the CD ratio.

items.statement: GNPA improved to 2.47% (down 28 bps YoY, 7 bps QoQ); NNPA improved to 1.14% (down from 1.24% QoQ, 1.39% YoY); PCR improved to 54.5%; SMA 1&2 at 4.78% (down from 5.47% YoY)
items.quote: Asset quality, showing consistent improvement during the quarter with gross NPA improved to 2.47%, improved by 28 basis points and by 7 basis points on year-on-year and quarter-on-quarter basis respectively. Net NPA has also improved significantly and now stood at 1.14%.

items.statement: Branch network expanded to 216 branches across 5 states and 2 UTs; focus on semi-urban and rural markets
items.quote: As of June '26, our branch network expanded to 216 branches across 5 states and 2 union territories, strengthening our presence in rural and semi-urban markets.

items.statement: Average CD ratio at 83% in Q1 FY27; targeting mid-to-high 80s over next 2-3 years to drive NIM expansion
items.quote: We are presently reporting an average CD ratio of 83%. And as we discussed over the last couple of calls, we intend to take it to the mid- to high 80s.

items.statement: Opex at 2.95-2.98% in Q1 FY27; expected to improve in FY27 as salary increments annualize and business scales; larger opex leverage expected in FY29
items.quote: Typically, current quarter, we're seeing at around 2.95% to 2.98% levels. That is the opex in the current quarter. I'm seeing an improvement in the coming period for this.

items.statement: No fund raise mentioned; capital adequacy at 21.6% provides ample headroom for growth
items.quote: Our balance sheet remained well capitalized and liquid. The capital adequacy ratio stood at 21.6%, providing sufficient headroom to support the future growth.

items.statement: Management explicitly states they do not provide guidance and prefer to be judged on actions rather than promises.
items.quote: We do not chase growth. That does not pay for itself. And as some of you have noticed in the past, occasionally with some frustration, we do not give guidance. We would rather you judge us by terms of what we do rather than what we promise.

items.statement: Management describes a soft market with declining pricing across lines, rising claims costs, and no TP rate hikes in 5 years, leading to a deliberate choice of profitability over growth.
items.quote: For 5 years, there has been no increase in third-party motor rates. Expense of management rules have pushed the commissions up. Pricing across most lines of business has drifted down, and now it is down across the board.

items.statement: Core profit after tax (with DAC, ex discounting & mark-to-market) fell 5% YoY to INR 190 cr; combined ratio worsened to 107.2% with DAC due to higher own damage loss ratio.
items.quote: So when we look at it from that perspective, our profit after tax with DAC, but without discounting and mark-to-market is INR190 crores compared to INR200 crores a year ago. This is a drop of 5%.

items.statement: Own damage loss ratio increased, driven by private car portfolio; corrective actions taken since February expected to stabilize OD loss ratio in Q2 FY27.
items.quote: Based on the actions which we have taken. And because the premium -- earned premium of previous quarters would flow quarter-by-quarter. And based on the actions we have taken in the other business we are writing, that earned premium will also flow quarter-by-quarter. We expect that our own damage loss ratio, which I ha

items.statement: Motor market share dropped to 5.6% from 6.25% YoY due to deliberate reduction in private car standalone OD and non-new cars, and commercial vehicles dropped to 23-24% of motor book; 2-wheeler new business grew 26%.
items.quote: Now reduction in motor market share is primarily due to the corrective actions we have taken essentially in private car, both stand-alone own damage section, about which I have spoken in the past and also non-new cars where we feel the combination of commission and the premium rates do not justify writing business in t

items.statement: Fire business de-grew 37% vs industry ~27-28% to protect gross loss ratios for reinsurers; gross fire loss ratio was 67% in Q1 despite one large claim.
items.quote: Despite that in quarter 1, the gross fire loss ratio is 67%. Now obviously, we don't know what will happen in future. But when we are looking at profitability of commercial line of business, we first look at gross and then look at net because on the net basis, loss ratio does not determine your profitability. It is on

items.statement: Net earned premium grew 8% YoY to INR 2,007 cr despite GWP declining 8%, reflecting earning through of prior premiums; long-term advance premium stands at INR 3,387 cr.
items.quote: Now this number has actually shown an increase of 8% compared to previous quarter last year to INR2,007 crores. So the premium is earning through, while the gross written premium has reduced.

items.statement: Expect motor OD loss ratio to stabilize in Q2 FY27 after corrective actions
items.quote: The business we started writing after taking correction still has to flow through, and then we expect it to become stable in own damage loss ratio sometime in the second quarter.

items.statement: Will consider dividend payment in Q4 FY27 board meeting based on IGAAP solvency and RBC norms
items.quote: We would take this up for discussion in the Board. If RBC comes and if our IFRS net worth is calculated into this account, then based on that, we'll be sitting on a huge surplus.

items.statement: 90-95% of vehicle segments need motor TP premium hike; not waiting for hike to act
items.quote: On a thumb rule, I would say 90%, 95% of the vehicles should see a hike in TP. But the question is, should we wait for it in the hope that it will increase this month, that month or you say right now, it increase hasn't happened and we'll go and run our business on that basis.

items.statement: Aggressively settling homemaker TP claims via compromise to mitigate legal inflation impact
items.quote: We will go out and aggressively settle homemakers compromises, particularly or specifically, we anyway settle, as I gave you a number, 83% of the claims on the TP side.

items.statement: Taking conservative underwriting actions by third week of August based on Supreme Court judgment
items.quote: Hopefully, Jasleen is confirming sometime in third week of August, we will be taking again, a conservative view of what the likely loss ratio will be, and we will take actions accordingly.

items.statement: 2-wheeler business growing 21-23% with 1+5 year long-term policies
items.quote: Within that, 2-wheeler business is 1 plus 5 2-wheeler is a business, which I said even in the first quarter, we are growing by 23%, 21%.

items.statement: Reducing motor TP market share since April; de-growing fire business by 37%
items.quote: In April, we started reducing the market share of TP. I would say with all humility that we understand this business better than most.

items.statement: Group health loss ratio elevated due to one large bank-driven PA policy with high intimations
items.quote: This quarter, the group level PA is essentially looking elevated because of one single large PA policy.

items.statement: No concept of MAD in P&L; reserves include frequency, legal inflation, and minimum wage hikes
items.quote: In the P&L or reserving, we have no concept of MAD. We provide, as I said, reserves on a basis where we include frequency, plus we include legal inflation.

items.statement: EOM ratio increase driven by mix shift from low-EOM fire/crop to motor and retention changes
items.quote: Overall EOM for every company, and you can look at the results would have gone up because low EOM business, especially fire and commercial lines has actually de-grown.

items.statement: Reserve conservatism shown: FY19 opening reserves INR204 cr reduced to INR132 cr over 7 years
items.quote: Just Ravi has shared with me for first year '18, '19, we started the year with INR204 crores. In 7 years later, we are at INR132 crores.

items.statement: Will provide detailed TP claim settlement update after 2 more quarters (6 months)
items.quote: We'll be happy to give a detailed update on this after 6 months, after 2 more quarters as to how we are settling these claims.

items.statement: Supports regulatory reforms reducing customer costs; expects distribution/commission/EOM changes this year
items.quote: I'm sure that now sometime this year, whether it is part of distribution reforms, part of commission or part of EOM framework, this year, a lot of these will actually get finalized.

items.statement: Not betting on TP hike, Supreme Court judgment reversal, or investment markets; acting conservatively now
items.quote: We are not taking a bet on TP hike. We are not taking a bet on Supreme Court judgment not holding. We are not taking a bet on investments. We are not taking a bet on markets premium rates going up.

items.statement: Management confident of delivering 35-40% AUM growth in FY27
items.quote: Based on the strong momentum we have built, we remain confident of delivering AUM growth of 35% to 40% growth during the current financial years.

items.statement: Targeting ROA of 3.5% for FY27 driven by higher-yield product mix
items.quote: Yes. So, we are targeting around 3.5% ROA for the FY27.

items.statement: Net interest margin expected to remain in 13-14% range for FY27
items.quote: So eventually net interest margin will remain in the range of 13% to 14%.

items.statement: Planning to raise INR100 crores via preference shares by September-October 2026
items.quote: And we are in a process of raising the capital. By September or latest by October, we will raise INR100 crores to for to manage our further growth and expansion.

items.statement: Two-wheeler share to decline from 84% to 75-77% by FY27 end via personal, top-up, used 2W, 3W, SBL growth
items.quote: And we are expecting that by end of this year it should be reach around 77% to -- 75% to 77%.

items.statement: MSME LAP expected to contribute 2-3% of AUM by FY27 end
items.quote: So that loan against property we are expecting around 3% by end of -- 2% to 3% because this year only we started.

items.statement: Technology spend to remain in similar range as percentage of expenses; significant spend on personal loan software this year
items.quote: So that will -- whenever need is arising, company is spending. And as far as total percentage of the entire expense is concerned, so it will remain what we are spending today, morely in the similar range only.

items.statement: Average cost of borrowing at 10.86%; Q1 increase due to holding INR200 crores liquidity
items.quote: On the funding side, our average cost of borrowing currently stands at 10.86%.

items.statement: Strong disbursement growth of 37% YoY to INR226 crores in Q1; Q2-Q3 expected to drive AUM jump due to festival season
items.quote: During the period, disbursement grew by 37% year-on-year to INR226 crores, reflecting a strong demand across the core vehicle finance portfolio and continued execution across existing market.

items.statement: Declared first interim dividend of INR0.25 per share (face value INR10) for FY27
items.quote: Further, the company declared first interim dividend of INR0.25 per equity shares on a face value of INR10 each for the financial year '26, '27, reflecting our continued commitment towards shareholders value creation.

items.statement: Battery replacement finance launched at INR60,000 ticket size for existing e-3W customers, with OEM tie-ups
items.quote: Yes. So, this is INR60,000 ticket size product. And basically after 15 months of utilization of three-wheeler, generally battery starts giving some issues and eventually the entire vehicle goes into that kind of situation where they generally, it becomes a non-performing asset.

items.statement: MSME LAP ticket size INR8-20 lakhs targeting shop-owning businessmen
items.quote: And the ticket size will be around will start from INR8 lakhs to INR20 lakhs. We are talking about the MSME LAP, right? So INR20 lakhs will be the highest loan which we are going to provide to the customers.

items.statement: FY27 revenue target INR 130-150 crore; FY27 turnover projection INR 220-250 crore
items.quote: we are estimating to get a turnover of around INR130 crores to INR150 crores somewhere in between for this financial

items.statement: PAT margin expected at 17-18% for FY27; Q1 EBITDA margin dip due to raw material invoicing timing
items.quote: we are estimating a margin of around 17% to 18% PAT year-on-year

items.statement: Q1 EBITDA margin fell from 40% to 20% YoY due to raw material purchase timing shift to Q1
items.quote: Last year, most of the raw material was purchased in Q4 of the previous year. This year, most of the raw material got purchased earlier but the stock got delivered only in Q1 time

items.statement: B2B/B2C mix to remain 70/30; ticket size per school increased from INR 1 lakh to INR 40 lakh via Pelican platform
items.quote: going forward, the mix is going to be same 70%, 30% but the turnovers will increase on both fronts

items.statement: Notebook manufacturing capacity at 10-20% of addressable demand; will add machines as scale grows; textbook printing at 80-85% capacity, sufficient up to INR 300 crore turnover
items.quote: right now we have the machines what we have for notebook can only sustain like 10% to 20% of the demand of 100% of our market wherever our presence is there

items.statement: Expanding into UP, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Assam; UP seen as most meaningful; targeting market share growth from 1-2% to 5% in new states over 3 years
items.quote: in the next three years, we are estimating to grow it to 5%

items.statement: Technology (LMS/AI) bundled free with textbooks; MRP increased by INR 10-12 per book to cover server and development costs
items.quote: I increased the MRP by another INR10 to INR12 and started giving this technology for free

items.statement: Curriculum changes occur every 20-30 years (last 2020 NEP); minor annual changes managed with early publisher intimation
items.quote: post-independence the curriculum was completely revamped three times, sir, so far. The last update was in 2020 when the New Education Policy was introduced

items.statement: Textbook prescriptions lock in 3-4 year recurring revenue per school; 13,000 schools currently supplied
items.quote: usually when a book gets prescribed in the school, it -- the business lasts for three to four years in that school

items.statement: Trade receivables INR 100 crore at Q1 end; 40%+ recovered by July-August; 90% by Oct-Nov; 7-10% over 6 months
items.quote: out of the INR100 crores more than 40% has been recovered by July and August. By October-November, 90% of the receivables will be recovered

items.statement: AUM growth guidance maintained at 25-30% for FY27
items.quote: We are targeting an AUM growth, as we had said in the guidance, between 25% to 30% for this year.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance maintained at 3.5-4% for FY27
items.quote: Our guidance on credit cost was, and at the beginning of the year we had given a guidance of 3.5% to 4%, and this appears well within our grasp now.

items.statement: NIM guidance maintained at 14.25-14.75% for FY27 despite Q1 beat
items.quote: From a NIM perspective, the guidance that we had given, we expect to stay on target.

items.statement: Opex ratio guidance maintained at 8.25-8.75% for FY27
items.quote: We did realize that quarter 1, quarter 2 we might be out of those bands and quarter 3, quarter 4 we will be very much in the band giving a result which for the entire year should be in that band.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 NIM improved 20bps sequentially to 15.9%
items.quote: Despite the increasing share of mortgage loans in our portfolio, our NIM actually improved by 20 basis points sequentially to 15.9%.

items.statement: Incremental borrowing cost at 10.2%, expected to drop 10-15bps further with rating upgrade
items.quote: Our incremental borrowing has been coming at nearly 60 bps lower and therefore my cost of the incremental borrowing that I'm doing today is at around 10.20%. This we expect with the credit upgrading, we expect to drop this further by around 10 to 15 bps.

items.statement: Borrowing cost expected to reduce 20-25bps on incremental borrowings due to rating upgrade
items.quote: It is expected to, on one hand, broaden our lender relationships and enhance funding flexibility, and on the other hand, it is also going to reduce our borrowing cost by approximately 20 to 25 basis points on the incremental borrowings over the course of the year.

items.statement: Strong demand environment for working capital from micro-MSMEs continues
items.quote: We have continued to see a constructive demand environment for working capital from our core market.

items.statement: Added 44,000 new borrowers in Q1 FY27, up 38% YoY despite tighter underwriting
items.quote: During this quarter, we added more than 44,000 new borrowers, which is a growth of 38% over the same period last year.

items.statement: Mortgage share at 22% of portfolio, expected to grow marginally in FY27
items.quote: While we are today already at 22% of our portfolio in mortgages, we expect it to only grow marginally through the year.

items.statement: Long-term target: 60-70% hypothecation, 30% Micro LAP, up to 10% other products (gold/solar) in 3 years
items.quote: We will like to see 60%-70% hypothecation, 30% Micro LAP, and at best 10% can be some other product, and this is over the next 3 years I would say.

items.statement: Plan to add 40-50 branches in FY27, focusing on deepening existing markets
items.quote: This year, our strategy remains focused on deepening our presence in existing markets rather than entering new geographies, and hence we expect to add only around 40 to 50 branches during the year.

items.statement: Domestic textile demand driven by state policies (Gujarat, Odisha, MP) and FTAs; gradual spindle absorption expected
items.quote: There are a lot of state policies which have come. Gujarat, Orissa and I think Madhya Pradesh. There's a specific region, Dhar region, I think, I think that is these are the policies which are kind of triggering a lot of activity within the order book.

items.statement: ATC new facility capex of Rs 150 crore for land and building over 18-24 months
items.quote: We are going to have I think 150 crores worth of land building being built. Building basically land is of course our own. So, building being built up for ATC and this, the timeline for this is over at least 18 to 24 months.

items.statement: ATC margins positively impacted by forex; mix shift to assemblies boosted Q1 margins
items.quote: ATC margin is positively impacted by Forex. In fact, if you see last quarter. And that is where probably the comparison. Is not very like to like there Was a huge jump last quarter from 85 to 95 and then of course. It has stayed somewhere in the range of 94, 96.

items.statement: MTD margins pressured by lower turnover; 75-80% capacity utilization with room for 15-20% more output
items.quote: With respect to mission tool division the capacity utilization will be in the region of 75 to 80%. We can still push out more machines. There will be capex which will be required for increasing it beyond which we Will be planning and we'll be investing In MTD as we go along but yes, we will be at around. 80% Capacity a

items.statement: Input costs up 3-3.5% due to commodities, fuel, logistics; price pass-through clauses exist in ATC/Foundry, being pursued in MTD
items.quote: If you want a number on that. It could be anywhere up from between three to three and a half percent where the costs would have, would be going up. That is the way we are looking at it.

items.statement: ATC order book mix shifting: currently 20% composite/80% metallic in revenue, 25% composite/75% metallic in order book
items.quote: From an order book Stand point, would be around 25% composite and 75% metallics. Composite again has to stabilize.

items.statement: ATC order book at Rs 1,000 crore for execution over 3-3.5 years, 90% export
items.quote: The order book for ATC is in the region of thousand crores of orders for execution over a period of three years, three to three and a half years. That is the order book of ATC for which is tied up for execution fully.

items.statement: Middle East tensions increasing commodity, fuel, gas, helium and transport costs; supply chain resilience maintained with 4-5 month material visibility
items.quote: All the costs, be it commodity, be it fuel, be it the gas and. A lot of these are being used. So, if you look at LPG, if you look at our sheet metal process, we use helium. If you look at So transport costs are up, commodity cost is up, everything is up to some extent.

items.statement: Enabling resolution passed for diversification into EV, pharma, specialty chemicals, advanced tech; no immediate plans
items.quote: The idea is that we are looking at various options which are available and this is an enablement resolution. Anything which is significant which needs to be informed, we'll bring it too, it will get published and it will get informed to the shareholders.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin expanded to 15.46%, up 1050 bps YoY and 400 bps QoQ, driven by volume growth, pricing actions, inventory gains, and renewable power.
items.quote: EBITDA margin improved significantly to 15.46%, representing an expansion of 1050 basis points year-on-year and 400 basis points over the previous quarter.

items.statement: Capex of over Rs 100 crore planned for FY27, focused on mother yarn capacity (commissioning FY28), value-added filament yarn products, renewable power at Bharuch, efficiency upgrades, and safety improvements.
items.quote: We expect to spend over 100 crores in CAPEX in the current year, current financial year.

items.statement: No fund raise mentioned; capex funded internally; healthy cash balance on balance sheet noted by analyst.
items.quote: One more question is about the healthy cash balance, which is there on the balance sheet. So, my question is regarding, if you could talk about the CAPEX plans for the company...

items.statement: Expects full-year performance to be 4.5x-5x Q1 results, consistent with historical pattern
items.quote: So typically, we see that the first quarter by the end of the year, it is not just multiplied by 4, but sometimes it is more like 4.5x to 5x that you will see at the end of the year. And that's what we are expecting this year also.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 capex was INR 5,300 crores; full-year target INR 25,000 crores with 50% for renewables
items.quote: On the capital expenditure, for the first time, we spent INR 5,300 crores in the first quarter. And we expect that the INR 25,000 crores that we have lined up for this year, we'll be able to implement.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 capex expected at INR 6,000-6,500 crores, half for renewables targeting 800-900 MW commissioning
items.quote: you can assume in our quarter 2 also, we're kind of looking at a capex plan of probably higher than INR 6,000 crores. Maybe if everything goes well, it will be closer to INR 6,500 crores.

items.statement: Renewable capacity addition target 2,500-2,700 MW in FY27; 200 MW commissioned, 500 MW imminent, crossing 9 GW by year-end
items.quote: Now this year, we will set up 2,500 megawatt to 2,700 megawatt. Already 200 was commissioned and another 500 will get commissioned in the next few weeks.

items.statement: TBCB transmission projects: Jalpura-Khurja line completing in days, Bikaner-Neemrana by October; revenues from Q2 onwards
items.quote: One will get completed, the Jalpura -Khurja line in the next few days. The other one, the Bikaner -Neemrana line will also get commissioned by October.

items.statement: Mumbai Transmission regulated investment pipeline INR 10,000 crores over 5 years with efficiency upsides
items.quote: we have a huge pipeline of investment, which is there in Mumbai transmission, nearly INR 10,000 crores of investment will happen in the next 5 years.

items.statement: Power demand grew 8.5% in Q1 FY27 (May 11%, June 9.8%); July sustained at 260-270 GW; long summer expected
items.quote: The power demand growth has been very strong in the first quarter. It was nearly 8.5% increase. In fact, in the month of May, it was nearly 11% and June was 9.8%.

items.statement: Rooftop solar revenue grew ~100% YoY in Q1; targeting 60-70% growth in FY27; cumulative INR 30,000 crores revenue by 2029
items.quote: In fact, last year, we grew by 100%, and this year also, we have plans to grow by about 60% to 70%.

items.statement: Module plant operating at full capacity (1,000 MW in Q1); cell production catching up after line change; margins ~25-26% sustained
items.quote: For the first time, our module plant we crossed 1,000 megawatt in the first quarter, and we expect that we have virtually peaked over there or peaking over there in terms of our module production.

items.statement: RE curtailment ~5% industry-wide in Q1; expected to settle in next few quarters as transmission lines progress
items.quote: there's been a general curtailment of roughly about 5%. And that we think is also the industry trend. But given that a lot of transmission lines and evacuation lines are in fast progression, we think that this curtailment will settle in, in the next few quarters.

items.statement: Indonesian coal prices up 5-7%; expect up to 5% increase over next 9 months; new export rules compliant, no major impact
items.quote: I would say about 5% to 7%. So in that range, the coal price increase. And we don't expect too much of changes happening. But yes, up to 5% over the next 9 months, you can expect.

items.statement: Pumped hydro: 1,000 MW (3x334 MW) commissioning from early CY2029; 1 unit via SECI annuity bid, 2 units in talks with Tata Steel/others
items.quote: We are doing very good construction work over there. And we expect that beginning of calendar year 2029, we will be in a position to commission the plant.

items.statement: Shirwata PSP 1,800 MW construction to start H2 FY27 after approvals; Khorlochhu 600 MW Bhutan hydro PPA signed with UPPCL, operational CY2030
items.quote: We have also tied up the PPA for 600 megawatt of Bhutan project, the Khorlochhu project with UPPCL. And the PPA has been signed with them, and it has got the regulatory approval.

items.statement: Mundra SPPA with Gujarat: cost-reflective tariff, fixed cost covered but no ROE; 3 state approvals expected August, 4th in September
items.quote: So presently, the supplementary PPA is on actual cost of coal, and all parameters, including heat rate, also will be on actual. So it's more towards cost reimbursement and cost reflective without any margin to be made from the plant.

items.statement: Target steady-state EBITDA of INR6,500 per metric ton for nutrient business once new plants commercialize
items.quote: Our average EBITDA, which used to be INR5,000 need to go up to INR6,500 per metric ton.

items.statement: Sustainable capex of INR300 crores annually; open to opportunistic investments with reasonable returns
items.quote: I would put a normal sustainable capex of INR300 crores would be the number we'll look at.

items.statement: High visibility of 8-9 million tons of nutrients (5 million tons fertilizer + 1 million tons trading + 1 million tons SSP + organic + urea/imported DAP) for next 2 years
items.quote: We have high visibility of 8 million to 9 million tons of nutrients. That I think will see us through for the next 2 years.

items.statement: Fertilizer margins under pressure due to elevated raw material costs not fully compensated by NBS subsidy rates
items.quote: Fertilizer business margins were under pressure due to sudden spurt in key input raw materials like ammonia and sulphur.

items.statement: Phosphatic fertilizer consumption stable in Q1; farmer sentiment cautious due to monsoon uncertainty; sowing momentum improving in July
items.quote: Consumption remained stable, especially farmers picking up lower MRP stocks in the first quarter and the industry maintained the same consumption sales volume of phosphatic fertilizer in the first quarter as compared to last year.

items.statement: SSP volumes grew 19% with premium products (GroPlus, Urea-SSP) constituting >50% of sales; Specialty Nutrients growing 25-30% with 20% EBITDA margin
items.quote: SSP business continued its strong growth trajectory with volumes increasing by 19% - we have been focusing on differentiated products like GroPlus and Urea-SSP, which constituted more than 50% of the total SSP sales.

items.statement: Sulphur prices structurally high due to EV battery demand; expected to remain elevated for some time but not sustainable
items.quote: Sulphur is actually against our initial expectation - sulphur is holding high. I think sulphur is likely to remain high for some time, but it's not sustainable.

items.statement: NP/NPK production down 21% and imports down 38% due to unviable subsidy rates; risk of impact in Q2 if subsidy not revised
items.quote: Domestic capacities cannot afford to produce at the high input prices of sulphur and ammonia. So its critical for the subsidy rates to get revised if the production has to come through otherwise, it can have an impact in Q2 as well.

items.statement: Granulation project on track for Q4 FY27 commissioning; MAP plant at Kakinada and seaweed granulation plant progressing; evaluating SSP facility in Senegal ($5-6M for 100-150K tons)
items.quote: Granulation project is progressing well - as planned, we are on track for commissioning this in Q4 of this year.

items.statement: Crop Protection exports and B2B sales drove 20% revenue growth to INR870 crores; domestic formulation softer due to delayed sowings
items.quote: Revenue grew by 20% year-on-year to INR870 crores, while EBIT increased 44% to INR159 crores, reflecting improved product mix, traction for its key molecules and the ability to pass on higher raw material costs in the export market.

items.statement: New products share in domestic B2C crop protection increased to 32% from 23%; 3 new products launched in Q1
items.quote: Share of sales in the new products in the domestic B2C stands at 32% as compared to 23% last year. We have also introduced 3 new products during the current quarter.

items.statement: Retail revenue up 85% YoY; 76% stores profitable vs 61% last year; network expanded to 1,200+ outlets with 22 new stores
items.quote: Revenue of retail business increased by 85% year-on-year, reflecting improved scale, operating leverage and profitability across the network. 76% of the stores were profitable during the quarter compared to 61% in the corresponding period last year.

items.statement: Nano DAP sales volume grew 2% with ~60% market share; exports initiated; growth moderated by bans in UP and Maharashtra
items.quote: The Nano business delivered stable performance with sales volume growing 2% year-on-year, supported by sustained demand for Nano DAP and a market leadership position with nearly 60% of market share.

items.statement: Management expects volume growth to track market growth of 4-5% and does not expect 23% revenue growth to continue every quarter
items.quote: I think bottom line, if I can grow same as the market, that would be a happy place for me.

items.statement: Markets remain robust and growing at 4-5% range; festival season expected to support near-term demand
items.quote: The markets that we operate in remain robust, and there are challenges still remaining with the political crisis, et cetera, and the raw material, but we are quite confident that the market will be growing in near future, especially with the festival season coming in the next few months.

items.statement: Raw material cost pass-through varies by contract (monthly/quarterly indexing); most Q2 impact passed on; transparent inventory sharing with customers
items.quote: In terms of passing of RM costs, again, it depends on our contract. Sometimes with our customers, we have quarterly price change -- index change contract. In some cases, we are able to change that pretty frequently.

items.statement: Growth driven 1/3 each by price, volume, mix; home care and liquid categories growing faster; blueloop adoption below 30% but asset utilization >70%
items.quote: The growth was driven by price, volume and product mix, almost 1/3 each of that. And roughly, when you're talking about 23% growth overall in net sales, it's pretty robust.

items.statement: Investing in modernization and productivity improvements to support organic growth; solar captive plant at Khopoli coming online in Q3 supplying ~50% power
items.quote: We are channeling some of that money into modernization and capex expenditure, et cetera, that we do internally for organic growth.

items.statement: Middle East crisis causing supply chain disruption and raw material volatility; inventory built up consciously to avoid stock-outs; geopolitical situation makes procurement hard but manageable
items.quote: We actually kind of covered ourselves a bit higher versus the previous periods because of the fact that we were seeing a lot of volatility in the markets from a commodity standpoint and the Middle East Asia situation.

items.statement: Export and domestic growth balanced at ~23% each; exports 30% of sales volume to SE Asia, Africa, Europe, Americas; duty stability improving
items.quote: Actually, 30% of our sales volume comes from exports. So we are already supplying to Southeast Asia, Africa, Europe as well as Americas.

items.statement: Volume growth high single-digit (~9%); no specific revenue run-rate guidance; land monetization not disclosed; no inorganic acquisition plans currently
items.quote: I can't give you exact volume number. But I can tell you it's a high single digit. So if I compare last year with this year, Hitesh, so just short of, let's say, double digit.

items.statement: Conductor division pending order book at INR10,190 crores with 56.8% export proportion; new orders received INR5,245 crores in Q1 FY27, 65.8% exports
items.quote: The pending order book stands at around INR10,190 crores with an export proportion of 56.8%. New orders received by the conductor division were INR5,245 crores in the quarter, of which exports contributed to 65.8%.

items.statement: Cable division pending order book at INR1,925 crores, up from INR1,653 crores a year ago
items.quote: The pending order today stands at INR1,925 crores. So it largely covers the plan or the requirement for the current -- for the coming quarter compared to INR1,653 crores from a year ago.

items.statement: Conductor EBITDA per ton INR53,418 vs INR43,688 YoY; Oil EBITDA per kL INR25,482 vs INR7,004 YoY; Cable EBITDA margin 10.6% up 60 bps YoY

items.quote: I think the volume contribution is almost about 50-60 percent and top 10 sellers, I think the concentration is less on the sell side. It could be about 40 percent but we have every day almost about eight to nine hundred participants who participate in this market.

items.statement: Targeting INR6,000-6,500 crores disbursement for FY27
items.quote: So, we are looking at anywhere between INR6,000 crores to INR6,500 crores.

items.statement: Maintaining credit cost guidance of 2.5-3% for FY27; net credit cost expected closer to 2%
items.quote: Very much. We are at, as I said, 2.1% for Q1 and the efforts are on to retain that.

items.statement: Opex target ~INR675 crores for FY27 (down from INR760 crores FY26); ~10% increase in FY28
items.quote: So against the last year full opex of about INR760-odd crores. I think we should be more around INR675 crores or so for the full year this year. And next year should be just a 10% increase on that.

items.statement: INR545 crores sanctioned under CGS scheme; INR200 crores utilized; more sanctions in pipeline
items.quote: We managed to garner around INR545 crores of sanction under the credit guarantee scheme, and sanctions are still coming, and there are quite a few sanctions in the pipeline as well.

items.statement: NIM improved to 12.5% from 9.9% QoQ; yield at 24.6% (target 25.25%); marginal cost of borrowing down to 11.3% from 12%
items.quote: With the improving trend in the yield and declining borrowing cost, our NIM improved to 12.5% compared to 9.9% in the previous quarter.

items.statement: CGS borrowing priced at ~10% or slightly above; overall cost of borrowing down to 12.8% from 13.2%
items.quote: Pricing is just about at 10% or a little over 10% because there are sub-10%, there are marginally over 10% as well.

items.statement: Balance rights issue INR200 crores (INR100 cr promoter, INR100 cr others) expected this quarter
items.quote: The balance rights issue money of INR200 crores, INR100 crores from the promoter and the balance INR100 crores from others who participated is expected this quarter, before the end of this quarter.

items.statement: NBFC AUM long-term CAGR target of 20-25% after 1-2 year transition
items.quote: So, our aim is to increase at an CAGR of about 20-25%.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue target Rs 6,000-8,000 crores in 5 years at 20% CAGR
items.quote: So, if we grow 20%, we will have revenue in five years' time around Rs. 6,000 to Rs. 8,000 crores.

items.statement: NBFC secured book now 75% of AUM, up 5% YoY; yields rising with mix shift
items.quote: So, as you will see, even at the end of quarter-end the secured book constitutes 75% of the AUM, which is slightly higher than the last quarter-ended and even year-on-year, the secured book has grown by 5%.

items.statement: NBFC borrowing cost down 25 bps in Q1; NIM expected to grow gradually
items.quote: So, regarding the interest rate, so basically in the current quarter, we had a reduction in our weighted cost of fund by around 25 basis points.

items.statement: Insurance gross premium Rs 759 crores in Q1, 90% from non-life segment
items.quote: The major segment is our non-life insurance, which contributes approximately 90% of the total premium.

items.statement: Mutual fund AUM grew 11.5% to Rs 4,787 crores; 92,129 active SIPs
items.quote: Our mutual fund AUM grew from 4,294 crores as on March '26 to Rs. 4,787 crores as on 30th June, representing a growth of approximately 11.5%.

items.statement: Insurance EBIT moderated due to manpower and distribution investments for reinsurance opportunity
items.quote: The moderated EBIT growth versus revenue reflects investments in distribution capacity and technology infrastructure to support the upcoming reinsurance opportunity following our composite broker upgrade.

items.statement: Stoxkart revenue quadrupled YoY to Rs 20 crores; added 26,000 subscription clients
items.quote: If you compare Q1 2025 to Q1 2026, it contributed around 20 crores. In Q1 2026, we contributed 20 crores in terms of revenue. And as number of clients, we opened around 26,000 clients in the quarter.

items.statement: Gift City business expanding; major player with good prospects
items.quote: Moreover, we are very optimistic about our Gift City businesses. This is expanding. So, in years to come, Gift City is having good prospects. And we are a major player in Gift City.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin expanded 100 bps YoY to 26.2% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: On a standalone basis, Q1 FY27 operational income stood at Rs. 273.4 crores, up 11.1% YoY, with an EBITDA of Rs. 71.5 crores, at a margin of 26.2%, an expansion of 100 basis points YoY.

items.statement: Expects employee cost growth of 22-24% for full year FY27 including ESOP expenses
items.quote: However, if you look at on a full year basis, including ESOP expenses, we expect that on a full year basis, employee cost growth can be in the range of 22% to 24%.

items.statement: Current quarter commission cost as % of revenue (56.2% standalone) is a steady-state number for projections
items.quote: Broadly, you can because it might depend on the composition between insurance and the mutual fund. But however, I think on a margin basis, probably you can consider this as a good number for your projection purpose.

items.statement: Monthly SIP book increased to INR1,240 crores in July from INR1,203 crores in June; SIP collections stable at INR1,147 crores in June
items.quote: Our monthly SIP book has further increased to around INR1,240 crores when I'm talking to you. This gives us confidence that SIP accretion remains on a healthy trajectory.

items.statement: Net sales resilient at INR3,790 crores in Q1 FY27, up 50% YoY; gaining market share vs industry
items.quote: At the same time, our net sales remained resilient at INR3,790 crores. This represents a healthy 50% year-on-year growth.

items.statement: PMS AUM grew 37% YoY to ~INR1,900 crores; bond distribution income more than doubled YoY; SIF AUM crossed INR500 crores with 1,323 certified distributors
items.quote: Average PMS AUM grew by 37% year-on-year, and now it stands at roughly about INR1,900 crores. And our income from bond distribution business has more than doubled compared to the same quarter last year.

items.statement: Plans to add ~30 new branches in FY27; >12 already operationalized in Q1
items.quote: We plan to add around 30 new branches during the year, of which almost more than 12 branches have already been operationalized during the quarter.

items.statement: Added ~600 distribution partners/month in Q1 FY27 vs 430/month in FY26; driven by existing distributors moving to platform post regulatory changes
items.quote: During the first quarter of current year, which is FY27, we added around 600 partners per month compared to monthly run rate of 430 in FY26.

items.statement: Direct-indirect AUM split roughly 10-90; 10% includes Indus, Karvy, old B2C and iFAST
items.quote: Direct AUM roughly about -- and the direct-indirect split would be roughly about you can say 90-10 kind of a thing. 90% of the AUM is serviced by partners and 10% includes the Indus, Karvy, Prudent's old B2C and iFAST.

items.statement: Positive on SEBI's mutual fund-only PMS at INR25 lakh ticket; evaluating acquisition or own license; no board decision yet
items.quote: But after looking to this INR25 lakh of ticket size and mutual fund only PMS, I think we are also finding it very, very important thing in our system because it might be very, very helpful for us to provide this kind of services to our retail.

items.statement: Treasury book of ~INR650 crores; evaluating value-accretive acquisition opportunities to strengthen distribution platform
items.quote: Finally, with a treasury book of around INR650 crores, we continue to evaluate value-accretive acquisition opportunities that can further strengthen our distribution platform.

items.statement: Current mutual fund yield (~88 bps gross, ~31 bps net) expected to hold for FY27; may decline 1-2 bps over medium term on new business
items.quote: Currently, whatever is the yield on our assets, we believe that this kind of margins would continue in the near future. Of course, over time, with the size of down the commercial will come down, but that is mainly on a new business.

items.statement: Reaffirmed 20% AUM growth guidance for FY27, expecting INR 6,500-6,800 crore disbursements for the year
items.quote: We will be somewhere around INR 6,500 crores to INR 6,800 crores, which will enable us to achieve our growth guidance of 20% very comfortably.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance for FY27 maintained at 1.7%-1.9%, trending toward 1.7%
items.quote: The guidance what we have given for the credit cost for this financial year, the credit cost will be in somewhere between 1.7% to 1.9%. But already the trend is lower than what we have said in the higher side. So you see the trend goes towards 1.7% more likely in the quarters to come.

items.statement: Gross NPA guidance to fall below 3% in FY27
items.quote: We have also clearly guided you on the gross NPAs, which will fall to sub 3%.

items.statement: Write-offs guided at INR 225-250 crore for FY27, running at ~INR 60 crore per quarter
items.quote: We should be seeing write-offs for the full year at somewhere around INR225 crores to INR 250 crores, which is largely the run rate that we did in the first quarter. We did about INR 60 crores of write-offs in the first quarter.

items.statement: Incremental cost of borrowing expected around 8.5%, with 10-15 bps further compression possible this year assuming no repo hikes
items.quote: My sense is, I think our incremental cost of borrowing should be somewhere around the 8.5% level, which means we still have another 20-30 basis points of compression that can come in the borrowings over the period.

items.statement: Spreads expected to remain flat at current levels for next few quarters assuming no policy rate changes
items.quote: Spread should largely remain flat to current levels for the next few quarters, assuming no policy actions.

items.statement: Target ticket-size mix: 25% at ~INR 3 lakh, 50% at ~INR 5 lakh, 25% at ~INR 10 lakh; average disbursement ticket ~INR 5 lakh
items.quote: We definitely want to operate at 25-50-20, which will be 25% at around INR3 lakh ticket size and 50% around the INR5 lakh ticket size and the other 25% closer to the INR10 lakh ticket size.

items.statement: Energy cost increases and regulatory liquidity decisions flagged as key external risks to monitor
items.quote: One is on the energy cost, which has gone up, which may even go up. Second is on the liquidity front, what the regulator is going to take a call on the price hike.

items.statement: Adequate borrowing lines available; holding INR 1,850 crore liquidity; ADB ECB tranche pending with hedging cost impact
items.quote: We are still holding close to INR 1,850 crores on the balance sheet. So it's still a sizable number. But the focus of the company will clearly be to ensure appropriate cost of funds. But at the same time, we will not compromise on the growth.

items.statement: Guidance for 25 bps opex reduction for FY27 maintained
items.quote: Cost of operations have been calibrated in a downward sloping curve and we continue our guidance of a 25-basis point reduction this year over the 150-basis point reduction we've delivered since listing.

items.statement: Spreads improved 39 bps Q-o-Q to 9.4%; NIMs at 10.6%
items.quote: Spreads, which improved by 39 bps at 9.4% driven by both a lower cost of borrowing and better pricing on the asset side. NIMs moved up by a similar basis point as spreads and stood at 10.6%.

items.statement: Co-origination mix reset to 10% from ~20% due to new RBI norms; expected to return to usual run rate from Q2
items.quote: Following the revised guidelines, the co-origination mix reset to 10%. This has since stabilized and we expect a return to the usual run rate from this quarter onwards.

items.statement: Credit cost expected to remain range-bound at 1.4%-1.5% for next two quarters
items.quote: We are penciling in that it will be range-bound in this current range. So, 1.4% or 1.5%, this is the range that we are looking at for at least next two quarters.

items.statement: Guidance for coming quarter unchanged on all fronts; ROE at 14.7%
items.quote: Our guidance for the coming quarter remains unchanged on all fronts. No surprises there, birds on the badminton court notwithstanding.

items.statement: No new products planned; focus on deepening existing geographies and improving execution in MSME and gold loans
items.quote: We don't want to, at this stage look at anything different or new. We will continue doing what we are doing. Hopefully we will do it better than what we have done so far.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance maintained at mid-teens for FY27; EBITDA margin expected broadly in line with FY26
items.quote: Overall, we expect the top line to grow in line with the stated guidance of mid -teens. We will continue to invest behind our core brands, super-premium to luxury portfolio and organizational capabilities while maintaining FY27 EBITDA margins broadly in line with FY 26.

items.statement: Management indicates potential upside to high-teens revenue growth and 18% EBITDA margin over 2 years
items.quote: I would rather want to step it up from mid -teens, it may go even higher to high teens and an EBITDA margin of 18%.

items.statement: India-UK FTA expected to improve margins by 70-80 bps in FY27 and 130-140 bps in FY28
items.quote: We expect the benefit to flow in second half of the year and would lead to about 70 to 80 basis points improvement in current financial year. For FY28 on a full year basis, it would help us in improving margins by 130 to 140 basis points.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 gross margin expanded 277 bps to 46%; like-to-like gross margin 48.4% (up 522 bps) excluding supply chain impact
items.quote: Gross margin expanded by 277 basis points to 46%, supported by a favorable input cost environment and early benefits from backward integration despite the temporary impact of global supply chain disruptions.

items.statement: ICONiQ White volume grew 33.8% YoY to 3.1M cases in Q1 FY27; targeting ~15M cases in FY27 vs 10.7M in FY26
items.quote: ICONiQ White is now operating at a meaningful scale supported by domestic market penetration, the defense channel, and an expanding international presence.

items.statement: Prestige & Above segment contribution increased to 48.2% of volume and 59.3% of value in Q1 FY27 vs 46.2% and 55.8% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: In Q1 FY '27, the Prestige & Above segment contributed 48.2% of volumes and 59.3% of value compared to 46.2% and 55.8% respectively in Q1 FY26.

items.statement: ABD Maestro luxury portfolio FY26 revenue ~₹40 crore; targeting 2x growth to ~₹80 crore in FY27
items.quote: The turnover that we clocked in FY 26 was top line of ~₹40 crores, which we expect to double in FY27.

items.statement: Global supply chain disruption impacted Q1 FY27 by ₹24 crore; management expects pressure only up to Q2 FY27 with recovery in H2
items.quote: I am extremely optimistic by saying that maximum that we would face pressure up to Q2. Q3 and Q4, we will all bounce back as an industry.

items.statement: Telangana government overdues ~₹400 crore; recent supplies paid on time, legacy overdues being cleared
items.quote: Overdue from Telangana government is approximate ₹400 crores. So right now, what's happening is Telangana is paying us well within agreed timeline for all recent supplies.

items.statement: Price increase dialogue ongoing with Telangana and 1-2 other states; management optimistic on materialization
items.quote: I personally feel that considering the first 2 quarters margin pressure, representations to most state governments that we have given, some state may also consider giving us price increases.

items.statement: Capex program to be funded through internal accruals and debt while maintaining leverage within defined framework
items.quote: Our capex program is planned to be funded through internal accruals and debt while maintaining leverage within our defined framework through the investment cycle.

items.statement: Reiterated FY28 outlook of $400 million organic revenue and 40% EBITDA margins
items.quote: we really remain confident and are happy to reiterate our FY28 outlook of $400 million organic revenue as well as, EBITDA margins of 40%.

items.statement: Q1 EBITDA margin improved significantly due to favorable mix from drug device combination business and H2-heavy base business
items.quote: it's basically the mix which is driving this. You know, the as you see there's a significant improvement in margins which primarily coming from higher contribution from the drug device combination business

items.statement: Demand for semaglutide generics significantly outpaces supply in Canada and India; customer forecasts remain robust
items.quote: The constraint in this market has been supply, not demand. In fact, the demand has been significantly outpacing supply both in the markets where the brand was present or was launching.

items.statement: Line 1 at ~225 sterile days/year at full revenue contribution in Q1; profitability not yet optimal due to upfronted opex for new lines
items.quote: we look at one line at about roughly 225 odd days, sterile days available. And based upon the per day realization for us, I would say that quarter one we had, reached fairly the full contribution which is there per line.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 8-12% YoY for FY27
items.quote: we foresee a growth of about 8% to 12% on a year on year basis on the revenue compared to last year from a growth perspective

items.statement: Medium-term revenue growth target of 8-12%
items.quote: These strengths support our medium-term target of delivering revenue growth of 8% to 12%.

items.statement: Capex plan of INR 140-160 crores for FY27
items.quote: we will probably maintain the range we have said earlier, about INR 140 crores to INR 160 crores per year of capital expenditure, even in this financial year

items.statement: Bengaluru metal card facility expected operational by end of calendar year 2026
items.quote: We expect the Bengaluru facility to be operational by the end of the calendar year after the necessary regulatory approvals.

items.statement: Won two multi-year PSU bank tenders worth INR 73 crores over tender period
items.quote: In this quarter, we won two multi-year tenders from leading PSU banks, which represent approximately INR 73 crores in revenue over the tender period.

items.statement: Gross margin moderated to 41.7% in Q1 FY27 from 44.5% in Q1 FY26 due to higher material costs
items.quote: Gross margin moderated to 41.7% in Q1 FY27 from 44.5% in Q1 FY26 as cost of materials consumed increased faster than revenue.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved 135 bps YoY to 25.1% in Q1 FY27 despite gross margin pressure
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter came in at INR 94 crores with an EBITDA margin of 25.1%, an increase of 135 bps Y-o-Y.

items.statement: 40-45% of gross margin impact from currency, rest from war-driven commodity/logistics costs
items.quote: maybe 40% to 45% of impact is directly attributable to currency, and the remaining probably is due to the direct impact of the war on the input costs.

items.statement: Actively working with customers on price revisions to protect margins
items.quote: we are actively working with customers on price revisions and taking steps to protect margins and maintain healthy profitability.

items.statement: Expect H2 FY27 stronger driven by seasonal BFSI pickup and steady communication/IoT momentum
items.quote: given the nature of our business, we expect H2 FY27 to be stronger driven by seasonal pickup in BFSI demand, and steady momentum in the communication and fulfillment businesses, and continued growth in the IoT segment.

items.statement: IoT solutions grew 145% YoY to 18% of revenue; payment solutions 5% YoY at 42%; communication & fulfillment 13% YoY at 40%
items.quote: IoT solutions contributed 18% to total revenue in Q1 FY27 and witnessed a growth of 145% on Y-o-Y basis.

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainties, currency fluctuations, and cost pressures creating near-term headwinds
items.quote: As of now, we operate in a challenging environment impacted by geopolitical uncertainties, currency fluctuations, and cost pressures.

items.statement: SIM card capacity utilization at ~40%; overall capacity utilization 65-70% average, peaks at 85-90%
items.quote: For the SIM card business, Pratik, we were close to around 40% capacity utilization.

items.statement: Order book stood at Rs 357.63 crore as of March 31, 2026, providing visibility beyond 24 months due to 3-5 year contract life cycles.
items.quote: As on 31st March 2026, our order books stood at Rs. 357.63 crores. Since our contracts are 3-5 years in life cycle, these order books provide visibility beyond 24 months.
